title: Pattern Headings: Plants and Crops
summary: Pattern list of free-floating subdivisions for headings for individual plants and crops and groups of plants and crops (including algae, fungi, lichens, and extinct and fossil plants, at all taxonomic levels); pattern heading Corn. Excludes Plants; Plants, Cultivated; Crops; Field crops. Section E is a table of topical subdivisions with May Subd Geog and usage notes (several marked "Not established under Corn"); section F lists form subdivisions, which LC catalogers no longer use (LCGFT instead) but which remain valid for other institutions.
validation_rules: The category covers headings for individual plants and crops and groups of plants and crops, including algae, fungi, and lichens, at all taxonomic levels, established using either common or scientific names, and headings for extinct and fossil plants (e.g. `Camellias`, `Eucalyptus alba`, `Rice`, `Basidiomycetes`, `Forage plants`, `Fruit`, `Weeds`, `Yeast fungi`, `Gymnosperms, Fossil`). (H 1180 sec. B)
The headings `Plants`, `Plants, Cultivated`, `Crops`, and `Field crops` are not in the category and do not take these subdivisions as pattern subdivisions. (H 1180 sec. C)

Any subdivision listed is free-floating under any heading in the category if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file; established variant phrases/subdivisions may exist. (H 1180 sec. D.1)

Only subdivisions marked "Yes" in the May Subd Geog column may be followed by a geographic subdivision; e.g. `--Aging`, `--Analysis`, `--Anatomy`, `--Classification`, `--Cytology`, `--Genetics`, `--Geographical distribution`, `--Growth`, `--Identification`, `--Marketing`, `--Morphology`, `--Nomenclature`, `--Origin`, `--Phylogeny`, `--Religious aspects`, `--Reproduction`, `--Roots`, `--Seedlings`, `--Ultrastructure` are not. (H 1180 sec. E)
Use `--Breeding` for controlled mating and selection of plants by humans; use `--Reproduction` for the physiological processes by which plants generate offspring of the same kind. (H 1180 sec. E)

Use `--Composition` for results of chemical analyses of plants (substances of unfixed composition); use `--Analysis` for methods of analyzing, or analyzing a sample, to determine presence or quantity of substances. (H 1180 sec. E)

`--Catalogs and collections` is `$x` (topical) for works about catalogs or collections of plants and `$v` (form) for the catalogs or collections themselves; likewise `--Classification` is `$x` for theory/methodology of classification and `$v` for works that consist of a systematic breakdown. (H 1180 secs. E, F)
`--Colonization` is used under individual plants and groups of plants for the establishment of a species in an area not currently occupied by it. (H 1180 sec. E)

`--Grading` is used under individual plants and groups of plants for division of commercial products into categories of uniform quality. `--Weed control` is used under individual crops and groups of crops. (H 1180 sec. E)

The following are not established under `Corn` but may be used under other plants as appropriate: `--Conservation`, `--Conservation--Law and legislation`, `--Effect of browsing on`, `--Effect of dredging on`, `--Effect of sediments on`, `--Effect of water levels on`, `--Effect of water waves on`, `--Odor`, `--Population regeneration`, `--Population viability analysis`, `--Reintroduction`, `--Seedlings--Effect of browsing on`, `--Spores`, `--Spores--Morphology`, `--Variation`, `--Vertical distribution` (e.g. `Grasses--Conservation`, `Ferns--Spores`, `Phytoplankton--Vertical distribution`). (H 1180 sec. E)

Subdivisions ending in `--Law and legislation` (`--Law and legislation`, `--Conservation--Law and legislation`, `--Control--Law and legislation`, `--Protection--Law and legislation`, `--Research--Law and legislation`) may be further subdivided per H 1154.5 (legal topics). (H 1180 sec. E)

`--Religious aspects` may be further subdivided by a religion or Christian denomination; each heading `[plant or crop]--Religious aspects--[name of religion or denomination]` must be editorially established. See H 1998. (H 1180 sec. E)
`--Virus diseases` and `--Wounds and injuries` may be further subdivided by subdivisions used under diseases. (H 1180 sec. E)

Form subdivisions valid under this pattern: `--Catalogs and collections` (May Subd Geog), `--Classification`, `--Diseases and pests--Identification`, `--Germplasm resources--Catalogs and collections` (May Subd Geog), `--Gift books`, `--Identification`, `--Nomenclature`, `--Nomenclature (Popular)`, `--Nomenclature (Popular)--French, [Italian, etc.]`, `--Seeds--Identification`. The combinations `--Diseases and pests--Identification`, `--Germplasm resources--Catalogs and collections`, `--Seeds--Identification` are used as form subdivisions under individual plants and groups of plants. (H 1180 sec. F)

[LC practice] LC catalogers no longer use the form subdivisions in sec. F; they assign LCGFT terms instead. These form subdivisions remain valid LCSH and other institutions may use them per local policy. (H 1180 sec. F; H 1075)
[LC practice] An exceptional variant form to be retained gets a UF reference from the free-floating form (H 195); otherwise propose a change (H 193). (H 1180 sec. D.2)

sections.heading: B. Types of headings covered by the pattern
sections.text:
Headings for individual plants and crops and groups of plants and crops, including algae, fungi, and lichens, at all taxonomic levels, established using either common or scientific names. The pattern also covers headings for extinct and fossil plants.

Examples:

```
Camellias
Eucalyptus alba
Rice
Basidiomycetes
Forage plants
Fruit
Weeds
Yeast fungi
Davis peppergrass
Franklinia
Gymnosperms, Fossil
```

sections.heading: C. Types of headings not covered
sections.text: The category does not include the headings *Plants*; *Plants, Cultivated*; *Crops*; and *Field crops*.

sections.heading: D.1. General rule
sections.text: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

sections.heading: D.2. LC practice
sections.text: If an exceptional variant form is to be retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form following the procedures in H 195 if the reference does not yet exist. Otherwise, submit a proposal to change the variant form along with all bibliographic records requiring correction following the procedures in H 193.

sections.heading: F. List of form subdivisions
sections.text:
LC practice: As stated in H 1075, Library of Congress catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. The form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by LC catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

| Subdivision | May Subd Geog | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| $v Catalogs and collections | Yes | Use as a form subdivision under plants for catalogs or collections of those plants. |
| $v Classification |  | Use as a form subdivision under plants for works that consist of a systematic breakdown of a subject into its constituent categories or subtopics. |
| $x Diseases and pests $v Identification |  | Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual plants and groups of plants. |
| $x Germplasm resources $v Catalogs and collections | Yes | Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual plants and groups of plants. |
| $v Gift books |  |  |
| $v Identification |  |  |
| $v Nomenclature |  |  |
| $v Nomenclature (Popular) |  |  |
| $v Nomenclature (Popular) $x French, [Italian, etc.] |  |  |
| $x Seeds $v Identification |  | Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual plants and groups of plants. |

list.scope: Free-floating subdivisions under headings for individual plants and crops and groups of plants and crops, including algae, fungi, and lichens, at all taxonomic levels (common or scientific names), and extinct and fossil plants; not Plants; Plants, Cultivated; Crops; Field crops.
general_notes: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.  Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, Library of Congress catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. The form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by LC catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

--breeding.notes: Use *--Breeding* for the controlled mating and selection of plants by humans, usually for the purpose of improving the species or variety. For works on the physiological processes by which plants generate offspring of the same kind, use *--Reproduction*.

--catalogs and collections.use_under: plants for works about catalogs or collections of those plants
plants for catalogs or collections of those plants

--classification.use_under: plants for works on the theory and/or methodology of creating a systematic breakdown of a subject into its constituent categories or subtopics
plants for works that consist of a systematic breakdown of a subject into its constituent categories or subtopics

--colonization.use_under: individual plants and groups of plants for works about the establishment of a species in an area not currently occupied by that species

--composition.use_under: natural substances of unfixed composition, including soils, plants, animals, farm products, etc., for the results of chemical analyses of those substances
--composition.notes: For works on the methods of analyzing substances, including individual chemicals and materials and individual plants and groups of plants, or analyzing a sample, to determine the presence or quantity of those substances, use the subdivision *--Analysis*.

--conservation.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Grasses--Conservation*.

--conservation--law and legislation.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Grasses--Conservation*. See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.

--control--law and legislation.notes: See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.

--effect of browsing on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Forest plants--Effect of browsing on*; *Trees--Seedlings--Effect of browsing on*.

--effect of dredging on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Aquatic plants--Effect of dredging on*.

--effect of sediments on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Aquatic plants--Effect of sediments on*.

--effect of water levels on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Helophytes–Effect of water levels on*.

--effect of water waves on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Helophytes–Effect of water waves on*.

--grading.use_under: individual plants and groups of plants for works on the division of commercial products into categories of uniform quality to facilitate marketing

--law and legislation.notes: See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.

--odor.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Petunias--Odor*.

--population regeneration.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Wetland plants--Population regeneration*.

--population viability analysis.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Grasses--Population viability analysis*.

--protection--law and legislation.notes: See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.

--reintroduction.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Grasses--Reintroduction*.

--religious aspects.notes: May be subdivided topically by a religion or Christian denomination. Editorially establish each heading of the type *[plant or crop]--Religious aspects--[name of religion or denomination]*. For instructions, see H 1998.

--reproduction.notes: Use *--Reproduction* for the physiological processes by which plants generate offspring of the same kind. Use *--Breeding* for the controlled mating and selection of plants by humans, usually for the purpose of improving the species or variety.

--research--law and legislation.notes: See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.

--seedlings--effect of browsing on.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Trees--Seedlings--Effect of browsing on*.

--spores.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Ferns--Spores*.

--variation.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Grasses--Variation*.

--vertical distribution.notes: Not established under *Corn*. Use under other plants as appropriate, for example, *Phytoplankton--Vertical distribution*.
